h: Record Breakers, Monks and Secret Agents
p: The motor museum began in 1952, when Lord Montagu put a handful of old cars on display in the front hall of Palace House in memory of his father, a motoring pioneer. It has grown into the National Motor Museum, and among the most eye-catching exhibits are the land speed record cars, including Donald Campbell's Bluebird, the kind of machines that make your jaw drop when you see the scale of them up close.

Beaulieu Abbey goes back to 1204, when King John founded it for Cistercian monks. After the Dissolution, the estate passed to the ancestors of the Montagu family, which is why house and abbey sit side by side. In the domus, the old lay brothers' building, an exhibition tells the story of monastic life.

There's a darker chapter to look out for as well. During the Second World War, the estate was used to train secret agents of the Special Operations Executive, and an exhibition explains how men and women were taught to work behind enemy lines. Teenagers especially tend to find this fascinating.

Wander into the village before or after your visit. The Beaulieu River flows past the mill pond, and you'll likely see ponies and donkeys ambling about as if they own the place, which in the New Forest they more or less do. Drive slowly on the forest roads. Exbury Gardens, famous for rhododendrons and azaleas, is a short drive away, and the harbour town of Lymington makes a smashing evening stop.
